note: Public scientific sanitizers. Inactive unless SCIBENCH_TRIGGER_LOG is set. See SCIENTIFIC_CHECKERS.md.

checkers.precondition: a valid protein sequence of standard amino acids, length >= 9
checkers.invariant: a fixed 9-residue sliding window over length L yields L - 9 + 1 scores
checkers.observation_point: after the flexibility loop, before returning scores
checkers.rationale: a windowed profile with the wrong length silently misaligns every downstream position

checkers.precondition: a valid standard protein sequence of length >= 10
checkers.invariant: the local profile is equivariant under sequence reversal: flexibility(reverse(s))[::-1] == flexibility(s)
checkers.observation_point: after the flexibility loop; the checker re-calls flexibility() on the reversed sequence
checkers.alarm: the reversed-input profile, reversed back, differs beyond 1e-9
checkers.rationale: the weight list is built to be applied symmetrically about the window centre, so the profile should not depend on which end of the sequence is read first

checkers.precondition: a valid protein sequence of residues present in a complete amino-acid scale dict
checkers.invariant: protein_scale(scale, window=1, edge=1) returns exactly [scale[r] for r in sequence]
checkers.observation_point: the checker independently re-calls protein_scale with window=1, edge=1 and compares the profile to the per-residue scale values
checkers.alarm: the window=1 call raises, or its profile differs from the residue scale values beyond 1e-9
checkers.rationale: the smallest valid window is a defined query whose answer is the scale itself; the current weight formula divides by window - 1 and cannot produce it

checkers.precondition: a valid standard protein sequence whose residues are all in the scale dict, an even positive window, 0 <= edge <= 1
checkers.invariant: the scale profile is equivariant under sequence reversal: protein_scale(reverse(s))[::-1] == protein_scale(s)
checkers.observation_point: after the scale loop; the checker re-calls protein_scale() on the reversed sequence
checkers.alarm: the reversed-input profile, reversed back, differs beyond 1e-9
checkers.rationale: the window weights are meant to be applied symmetrically, but the middle-residue index the loop uses is off-centre for even windows

checkers.precondition: any in-frame coding DNA sequence over the index's genetic code (length a multiple of 3, letters ACGT). No restriction on codon composition.
checkers.invariant: CAI is the geometric mean of per-codon relative adaptiveness values w_ij in (0,1], so CAI is well-defined and lies in (0,1]; and replacing any codon by the highest-w_ij synonym of the same amino acid cannot decrease CAI
checkers.observation_point: after CodonAdaptationIndex.calculate computes the result (or raises), before returning
checkers.alarm: the result is undefined/non-finite, or CAI <= 0 or CAI > 1, or the CAI of the synonymously optimised sequence is lower than the CAI of the input (by > 1e-9)
checkers.rationale: CAI in (0,1] and monotone improvement toward the optimal synonymous sequence are definitional properties of the metric; a violation means the adaptiveness table or the geometric mean is being applied inconsistently

checkers.scientific_quantity: isoelectric point (pI) and net charge at pI
checkers.precondition: any sequence of standard amino acids (ACDEFGHIKLMNPQRSTVWY). No restriction on composition.
checkers.invariant: the isoelectric point is by definition the pH at which the modelled net charge is zero, so charge_at_pH(reported_pI) == 0
checkers.observation_point: after IsoelectricPoint.pi returns, evaluating the model net charge at the returned pH
checkers.rationale: if the reported pI does not zero the net charge it is not the isoelectric point; the value cannot be used for charge-based separation or 2D-gel prediction

checkers.precondition: a non-empty valid protein sequence and finite pH values in [0, 14]
checkers.invariant: net charge is monotonically non-increasing as pH rises
checkers.observation_point: in isoelectric_point(); the checker sweeps charge_at_pH over a 0.25-pH grid
checkers.alarm: a higher pH yields a greater net charge beyond 1e-9
checkers.rationale: Henderson-Hasselbalch partial charges are individually monotone in pH; the sum must be too

checkers.precondition: an unambiguous DNA sequence of length >= 4. Built-in value sets 1-8 all have empirical GC coefficient B > 0; if the caller overrides coefficients via userset=(A,B,C,D) with B <= 0 the premise is inverted and the check does not apply.
checkers.invariant: at fixed length, raising %GC does not lower Tm_GC (empirical B > 0)
checkers.observation_point: before returning melting_temp; the checker calls Tm_GC on all-A and all-G sequences of the same length
checkers.alarm: the all-A Tm exceeds this sequence's Tm, or exceeds the all-G Tm, beyond 1e-6
checkers.rationale: every published Tm_GC value set has a positive %GC coefficient

checkers.precondition: a single-stranded, non-circular DNA or RNA sequence of length >= 2 over ACGTU; checked at k = 1, L//2 and L-1
checkers.invariant: forming the backbone bond that joins two oligomers releases exactly one water, so for a single strand and any split point k in 1..L-1: MW(s) == MW(s[:k]) + MW(s[k:]) - water
checkers.observation_point: after molecular_weight returns; the checker re-calls it on each half
checkers.alarm: |MW(s) - (MW(s[:k]) + MW(s[k:]) - water)| > 1e-6 for any tested split point k
checkers.rationale: mass is additive over concatenation up to the condensation water at the new bond

checkers.precondition: any peptide of standard amino acids with length >= 3 (all DIWV dipeptide keys present); checked at the midpoint split
checkers.invariant: the instability index is a length-weighted sum of consecutive-residue DIWV terms, so L*II(s) == kA*II(s[:k]) + kB*II(s[k:]) + 10*DIWV[s[k-1]][s[k]] for every split point k
checkers.observation_point: after instability_index computes the value; the checker re-calls the API on the two halves
checkers.rationale: the dipeptide decomposition is a general additivity law for the index; a violation means the windowed sum or the length normalisation is wrong

checkers.precondition: DNA primer (>=2 nt, ACGT/U only), c_seq/shift/selfcomp/custom nn_table not set. The invariance check re-calls Tm_NN forwarding every result-affecting argument including dnac1/dnac2.
checkers.invariant: Tm_NN(seq) == Tm_NN(reverse_complement(seq)) with every other argument identical
checkers.observation_point: before returning melting_temp; the checker re-calls Tm_NN on the reverse complement with the same salt parameters
checkers.rationale: a perfect duplex has the same nearest-neighbor stack set read from either strand

checkers.precondition: DNA primer (>=2 nt, ACGT/U only), saltcorr in 1-4, K/Tris/Mg/dNTPs not set, Na>0. The monotonicity check re-calls Tm_NN forwarding dnac1/dnac2 and varies only [Na+].
checkers.invariant: raising [Na+] does not lower Tm_NN
checkers.observation_point: before returning melting_temp; the checker re-calls Tm_NN at half and double [Na+]
checkers.alarm: the doubled-[Na+] Tm is below this Tm, or this Tm is below the halved-[Na+] Tm, beyond 1e-6
checkers.rationale: counter-ions screen backbone charge and stabilise the duplex; every salt-correction method 1-4 is increasing in log[Na+]

checkers.precondition: method in {1, 3, 4}, only Na set (K=Tris=Mg=dNTPs=0), Na > 0
checkers.invariant: the term is k * log10([Na+] in M): monotonically increasing in [Na+] and exactly 0 at [Na+] = 1 M
checkers.observation_point: before returning corr; the checker re-calls salt_correction at half [Na+], double [Na+], and 1 M
checkers.alarm: corr is not between the half- and double-[Na+] values, or the 1 M value is not 0
checkers.rationale: methods 1/3/4 are pure logarithms of ionic strength; method 2 has a saturation term and is intentionally excluded

checkers.precondition: an unambiguous DNA sequence and a positive window
checkers.invariant: GC_skew(complement(seq)) is the element-wise negation of GC_skew(seq)
checkers.observation_point: before returning; the checker re-calls GC_skew on the (non-reversed) complement
checkers.alarm: any window's complement skew is not the negation of the original beyond 1e-9
checkers.rationale: complementing swaps G and C counts in every window, flipping the sign of G - C

checkers.precondition: a valid protein sequence of length >= 2; the second call uses the same monoisotopic flag
checkers.invariant: the mass is invariant under residue permutation
checkers.observation_point: after computing the mass; the checker re-calls molecular_weight on the reversed sequence
checkers.rationale: mass is a composition sum minus (n - 1) condensation waters, independent of order

checkers.precondition: an unambiguous single-stranded linear sequence of A/C/G/U, evaluated as RNA
checkers.invariant: the RNA mass exceeds the mass of the corresponding DNA string (U to T)
checkers.observation_point: after the mass calculation; the checker re-calls molecular_weight on the T-substituted string as DNA
checkers.alarm: the RNA mass is not greater than the DNA mass
checkers.rationale: per residue the ribose ring adds a 2'-oxygen that outweighs the thymine 5-methyl lost when T becomes U, so RNA of a given base string is heavier than the DNA of the same string

checkers.precondition: three distinct Vector points
checkers.invariant: calc_angle(v1, v2, v3) == calc_angle(v3, v2, v1)
checkers.observation_point: before returning; the checker re-calls calc_angle with the endpoints swapped
checkers.rationale: the angle at a vertex does not depend on which arm is named first

checkers.precondition: three Vector points, pairwise separated by at least ~1e-6 of the coordinate scale (below that the rigid-motion probe's own arithmetic loses the geometry)
checkers.invariant: the angle is unchanged by applying one rigid rotation plus translation to all three points
checkers.observation_point: before returning; the checker re-computes calc_angle on the transformed points
checkers.rationale: bond angles are Euclidean invariants

checkers.precondition: Four atoms, no three collinear and the geometry not planar-trans (|dihedral| != pi, where the atan2 branch cut makes +pi/-pi interchangeable under a proper rigid motion).
checkers.invariant: the dihedral is unchanged by one rigid rotation plus translation of all four points
checkers.observation_point: before returning; the checker re-computes calc_dihedral on the transformed points
checkers.rationale: torsion angles are invariant under proper rigid motions

checkers.precondition: Same as BP-PDB-006: a proper (non-degenerate, non-branch-cut) dihedral.
checkers.invariant: reflecting all four points (z -> -z) negates the signed dihedral
checkers.observation_point: before returning; the checker re-computes calc_dihedral on the mirrored points
checkers.alarm: the mirrored dihedral is not the negation of the original beyond 1e-7 (and the angle is not +/- pi)
checkers.rationale: a torsion angle is a pseudoscalar; an improper transformation flips its sign

checkers.precondition: two non-zero, non-collinear Vectors p, q (the antiparallel case p = -k q is a documented rotmat singularity and is excluded)
checkers.invariant: rotmat(p, q) is orthogonal with determinant +1
checkers.observation_point: before returning the matrix
checkers.alarm: R @ R.T is not the identity, or det(R) != 1, beyond 1e-9
checkers.rationale: a proper rotation preserves lengths and orientation

checkers.precondition: two non-zero Vectors p, q
checkers.invariant: p.left_multiply(rotmat(p, q)) points along q and has the same norm as p
checkers.observation_point: before returning the matrix
checkers.alarm: the rotated p is not parallel to q, or its norm changed, beyond 1e-7
checkers.rationale: rotmat is documented to rotate p onto q

checkers.precondition: two matching Nx3 coordinate arrays with N >= 3
checkers.invariant: the optimal RMSD is unchanged by a rigid motion of the moving set, and rms(A, B) == rms(B, A)
checkers.observation_point: after run(); the checker re-runs QCP on the rigidly moved moving set and on the swapped pair
checkers.alarm: either re-run's RMSD differs from this one beyond 1e-6
checkers.rationale: the optimal superposition distance is a metric on shapes, invariant to pose and symmetric

checkers.precondition: two equal-length lists of >=3 atoms whose coordinates are not all collinear
checkers.invariant: the rotation returned by the SVD superposition is a proper rotation: R^T R = I and det(R) = +1
checkers.observation_point: after SVDSuperimposer.run(), before Superimposer.set_atoms returns
checkers.rationale: a reflection (det -1) superposes mirror-image structures and would make an enantiomer look identical to its mirror

checkers.precondition: two equal-length, non-collinear atom lists RMSD comparison tolerance scales with the coordinate magnitude.
checkers.invariant: the optimal-superposition RMSD is unchanged when the moving coordinates are first transformed by an arbitrary rigid motion
checkers.observation_point: after SVDSuperimposer.run(), before set_atoms returns
checkers.rationale: the least-squares superposition distance is an intrinsic property of the two shapes and cannot depend on their initial placement

checkers.precondition: two equal-length, non-collinear atom lists
checkers.invariant: the optimal-superposition RMSD is symmetric in its two arguments: rms(A, B) = rms(B, A)
checkers.observation_point: after SVDSuperimposer.run(), before set_atoms returns
checkers.rationale: superposition RMSD is a metric on conformations; asymmetry means the centroid or normalisation handling differs between the two roles

checkers.precondition: the moving atom list is an exact rigid image of the fixed atom list (>=3 non-collinear atoms) RMSD comparison tolerance scales with the coordinate magnitude.
checkers.invariant: the optimal-superposition RMSD is 0
checkers.observation_point: after SVDSuperimposer.run(), before set_atoms returns
checkers.rationale: two structures that are congruent by a rigid motion must be superposable to zero; a non-zero result means the algorithm missed a known exact solution (e.g. the SVD sign branch)

checkers.precondition: two equal-length, non-collinear atom lists RMSD comparison tolerance scales with the coordinate magnitude.
checkers.invariant: applying the same row permutation to both atom lists leaves the optimal-superposition RMSD unchanged
checkers.observation_point: after SVDSuperimposer.run(), before set_atoms returns
checkers.rationale: RMSD sums over paired points; a dependence on enumeration order means an index-order assumption has leaked into the computation

checkers.precondition: mode='global'; a symmetric scoring scheme (scalar match/mismatch or a symmetric substitution matrix; target-side and query-side gap scores equal); two non-empty sequences
checkers.invariant: score(A, B) = score(B, A)
checkers.observation_point: after PairwiseAligner.score computes the score, before it returns
checkers.rationale: under a symmetric scoring model the optimal alignment score is a symmetric function of the sequence pair; asymmetry means target/query gap or matrix indexing is not even-handed and homology calls depend on argument order

checkers.precondition: score() vs align() agreement, for scoring schemes whose smallest term is well above the aligner's traceback epsilon (default 1e-6); below it the two paths legitimately diverge.
checkers.invariant: the score reported by score() equals the score of the best alignment returned by align()
checkers.observation_point: after PairwiseAligner.align builds the alignments, before returning
checkers.rationale: the score-only dynamic program and the traceback share an optimum by construction; a discrepancy means one of the two recurrences is wrong

checkers.precondition: mode='global'; symmetric scoring scheme; left-end and right-end gap scores equal; two non-empty sequences
checkers.invariant: score(A, B) = score(reverse(A), reverse(B))
checkers.observation_point: after PairwiseAligner.score computes the score, before it returns
checkers.rationale: reversing both sequences transposes the dynamic-programming matrix; a change in the global score means the left/right boundary gap handling is asymmetric

checkers.precondition: mode='global'; a symmetric substitution matrix is set; equal target/query gap scores; two non-empty sequences
checkers.invariant: replacing the substitution matrix with its transpose does not change the score
checkers.observation_point: after PairwiseAligner.score computes the score, before it returns
checkers.rationale: for a symmetric substitution model the matrix transpose is the identity operation; a difference means the aligner indexes the matrix as M[a][b] where it should use M[b][a] (or vice versa)

checkers.precondition: an ADDITIVE DistanceMatrix (input distances exactly realisable as path lengths on a weighted tree) with >= 4 taxa; the NJ main branch (n>2). Non-additive input is out of scope: tied Q-matrix minima make several NJ trees equally valid there.
checkers.invariant: for additive input, permuting the rows/columns of the matrix yields a tree with identical patristic distances between every pair of leaves
checkers.observation_point: after nj() builds the tree, before returning
checkers.alarm: additive input and any leaf-pair patristic distance differs by > 1e-6 between the tree and the tree built from a row/col-permuted copy
checkers.rationale: for additive data NJ reconstructs the unique generating tree; an order dependence then means the join sequence is decided by an implementation artefact rather than the data

checkers.precondition: Input distance matrix (n>=4) that is additive, decided directly on the input by an EXACT four-point condition plus the triangle inequality (tolerance ~1e-12 relative to the coordinate scale, not a fixed fudge).
checkers.invariant: for additive input, NJ reconstructs the generating tree exactly: every output patristic distance equals the corresponding input distance
checkers.observation_point: after nj() builds the tree, before returning
checkers.alarm: additive input and an output patristic distance differs from the input distance by > 1e-6
checkers.rationale: exact reconstruction on additive data is the correctness theorem for NJ (Saitou-Nei 1987; Studier-Keppler 1988); a deviation means NJ failed on an input it provably handles

checkers.precondition: a DistanceMatrix with >= 3 taxa; UPGMA output
checkers.invariant: the tree is ultrametric: all leaves equidistant from the root, and for any three leaves the two largest pairwise patristic distances are equal (three-point condition)
checkers.observation_point: after upgma() builds the tree, before returning
checkers.alarm: a root-to-leaf depth differs by > 1e-6, or the two largest of a leaf triple's pairwise patristic distances differ by > 1e-6
checkers.rationale: UPGMA assumes a molecular clock; a non-ultrametric result cannot be read as a clock-like divergence history, which is the modelling premise of the method

checkers.scientific_quantity: estimated branch length (expected substitutions per site)
checkers.precondition: UPGMA on any valid distance matrix; or NJ when the input matrix is additive, decided directly on the input by the four-point condition together with the triangle inequality (a non-negative tree metric is a metric). NJ negative branch lengths on non-additive input are documented, expected behaviour and out of scope.
checkers.invariant: every estimated branch length is >= 0
checkers.observation_point: after the tree is built, before returning
checkers.rationale: a negative branch length is negative evolutionary change; it has no biological meaning and corrupts every length-weighted downstream analysis (patristic distance, rate and date estimation, ancestral reconstruction)

checkers.precondition: a DNA PSSM (ACGT); a sequence at least as long as the motif with only ACGT; score at offset 0
checkers.invariant: the site score equals the sum of the per-position log-odds entries pssm[seq[i]][i]
checkers.observation_point: after _pwm.calculate fills the score array, before calculate() returns
checkers.rationale: positional independence (a sum of per-column log-odds) is the defining assumption of the PSSM model; the C routine and a direct sum are independent implementations of it and a mismatch means the reported score is not the model log-odds

checkers.precondition: a DNA PSSM; any ACGT query sequence; pssm.min and pssm.max finite
checkers.invariant: every site score lies in [pssm.min, pssm.max]
checkers.observation_point: after _pwm.calculate fills the score array, before calculate() returns
checkers.alarm: a returned score is < pssm.min - 1e-6 or > pssm.max + 1e-6
checkers.rationale: pssm.max is the consensus score and pssm.min the anticonsensus score; threshold-based motif search and score-to-p-value mapping rely on these bounds, so a score outside them cannot be placed on the motif's score distribution

checkers.precondition: a DNA PSSM; a query sequence exactly the motif length with only ACGT
checkers.invariant: score(S) with the PSSM equals score(reverse-complement(S)) with reverse_complement(PSSM)
checkers.observation_point: after _pwm.calculate fills the score array, before calculate() returns
checkers.rationale: a binding site can occur on either strand; the forward and reverse-complement scorings describe the same physical binding event, so an asymmetry biases every both-strands genome scan by strand

checkers.precondition: the average-mass path of molecular_weight (monoisotopic=False); any call
checkers.invariant: the hard-coded average condensation water 18.0153 equals 2*H + O from IUPACData.atom_weights (the standard atomic-weight table used elsewhere in Biopython)
checkers.observation_point: entry of molecular_weight, before the residue sum
checkers.rationale: a formula constant that disagrees with the module's own element table silently biases every molecular weight by a fixed offset per residue
